claims.statement: The package.json repository field must match the project's GitHub repository URL in this package flow; the illustrative HTTPS .git URL is not a real target, provenance proof or authorization to change configuration.
Published packages can subsequently be viewed on GitHub; a viewing-guide link is not a publication or access receipt and does not count the linked guide as reviewed.

For granular-permission registries, package admins can select private/public visibility and separately grant package access from organization/repository permissions. The linked registry matrix remains separate review work; package authority is not universal repository admin or rights to publish.

Most registries require personal-token or GITHUB_TOKEN authentication to pull public or private packages; public Container Registry packages specifically allow anonymous pulls. This token-generic statement does not independently establish fine-grained PAT compatibility.

In the pinned inheritance feature scope, FPT/GHEC, repository-linked publication inherits permissions by default. Inherited permissions must be removed to access granular settings; organization owners may disable automatic inheritance for new organization-scoped packages. No inheritance state or grant was changed.

Publishers automatically receive package admin; organization owners also receive admin for packages published to their organization. Personal-scoped packages may assign any person an access role, whereas organization-scoped packages may assign people or teams in that organization; no identities or effective assignments verified.

Actions package management grants an access role to the workflow repository using the GHES Actions access menu or the other-branch Add Repository button under Manage Actions access, as resolved from package_registry variables. Navigation and configurable roles are not verified access.

Read allows package download and metadata read. Write adds upload and metadata write. Admin additionally allows deletion, package management and permission grants. Preserve package-specific role semantics rather than substituting repository roles or authorization to delete.

The included note describes Actions REST deletion/restoration as public preview subject to change. The preview statement and role matrix do not prove sufficient token permissions, authorized mutation, successful restoration or actual enforcement.
